correctness.rationale: The largest label must be one consecutive k-block, so its observable incoming/outgoing pair counts force a unique reduced profile. Cross-label pairs cannot repeat by Stirling noninterlacing, while aa counts are at most k-1. Inverse fibers therefore multiply by one at an endpoint or the reduced ab multiplicity internally. This proves the universal bound (k-1)^(n-1), its unique extremal profile for k>=3, and n! block-concatenation singleton profiles. The normalized n!/product(kj+1) and gamma asymptotic follow. Exhaustive direct source enumeration and a separately implemented profile-only recurrence both passed all stated finite parameter sets; no finite result was treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: For every k and n, the theorem solves the actual inverse-list sizes of an oriented two-gram readout on a classical nested multipermutation class, with a sharp exponential worst fiber and a complete constructive characterization of the n! uniquely decodable words for k>=3. It quantitatively identifies information loss and supplies a reconstruction algorithm, beyond merely restating standard word-count or small-case sequence data. Unrestricted reconstruction, higher read lengths and total profile counts remain outside scope.
